name: aeg-d-strong-lensing
title: Galaxy-scale strong lenses: projected mass inside the Einstein radius against projected stars and gas in the same cylinder
description: Atlas re-issue of aeg-d-strong-lensing/v1 under data standard 2.5.1 (D-083, D-084): the same 147 rows and values as v1 (one projected g_obs and g_bar per lens at the Einstein radius, D-064), with the uncertainty terms read at source in step A, confidence levels, and two corrections to how uncertainties are carried (known issue #139). (1) The Einstein-radius (θ_E) error moves from g_obs to g_bar (standard §2a rule 7; adjudication F1): where M_E is the mass inside the radius of mean convergence 1, g_obs = π G Σ_cr does not depend on θ_E, so a θ_E error moves g_bar and R_E, not g_obs; v1 carried it on g_obs "at fixed R_E". (2) Distance enters g_obs at first order (D-094, replacing D-064 item 4; F2): g_obs ∝ H0 at fixed Ω_m and ∝ 1/D_l for a lens-distance change, while the stellar g_bar is distance-free; the H0 pairs and peculiar-velocity sizes the sources state are uncertainty terms (D-104 rule 1). Where no single-component light profile is printed (the two MaNGA lenses, NGC 6505 and J0403−0239): θ_E error stated; effect on g_bar not computed (D-104 rule 3). The central black hole is not added to g_bar (D-104 rule 2): every size the sources quote comes from an M_BH–σ scaling of the lens's own velocity dispersion, an input from the system's own kinematics; R28 sizes it at "2 per cent of M_Ein" for SNL-0 (lensz_arXiv.tex l. 693), which is a larger share of M*(<R_E), and so of g_bar, because M* is only part of M_Ein. No value changes: the frozen second reading found no source-stated preferred value or exclusion that differs from v1 (D-096). See REPRODUCTION.md, REPRODUCTION_RESULT.md and SECOND_READING.md; v1's tests and checks stand for the unchanged values.
